full_judgment:
2. Plaintiffs are the petitioners in this application. It is their case that they filed a suit being Title Suit No. 35 of 1986 in the Court of the learned Subordinate Judge, Faridpur for partitioning the suit land. The plaintiffs after filing the suit, filed an application under Order 39 rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for temporary injunction restraining the defendants from making any pucca construction in the suit land until it is partitioned. It is their case that by three registered sale deeds they purchased 16 decimals of land in plot No. 811. The total area of the plot is more or less 50 decimals. They also took settlement 9 decimals of land from the vested and non-resident property authority. In total they are possessing and enjoying 25 decimals of land. The defendant Nos. 1 to 8 purchased the remaining portion of the suit plot and defendant No. 1 took lease some portion of the said plot from the vested and non-resident property authority Though the suit plot has not been partitioned amongst the co-sharers, the defendants were trying to construct building on the valuable portion of the above plot. So they were compelled to file above suit with a prayer for temporary injunction. 

 3. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the application for temporary injunction by filing written objection. It is their case that they acquired 18 decimals of land out of total 50 decimals by purchase from the admitted owners and also by taking lease from the vested property authority. These defendants have been possessing 18 decimals in the northern portion of the said plot No. 811. They purchased the above portion in 1976 and since then they have been possessing the same. They took loan from the House Building Finance Corporation for construction of multistoried building there. In some portion of the suit plot they have in fact constructed a building at a huge amount of money. The defendants have never encroached upon any portion of the land of the plaintiffs and after purchasing the land in 1976 they started construction and completed it upto roof level of the building. They had no intention to cause any loss to the plaintiffs. Since they are making construction on their own land, the plaintiffs have no prima-facie case for obtaining an order of injunction. 

 4. After perusing the materials on record and hearing the parties, the learned Subordinate Judge rejected the prayer for injunction by his judgment and order dated 10.1.87. Against the aforesaid judgment and order the plaintiffs preferred an appeal being Misc. Appeal No. 12 of 1987. The learned District Judge, after hearing the parties and perusing the materials on record, dismissed the appeal affirming the judgment and order of the learned Subordinate Judge. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and order of the learned District Judge the petitioners preferred this revisional application and obtained the present Rule. 

 5. Mr. AFM Ali Asgar, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, submits that the defendants have encroached upon some portion of the land of the plaintiffs and started construction of building in the suit land which will change its nature and character. If the defendants are allowed to construct the building they will suffer irreparable loss and injury. It is an admitted position that the suit land contains 50 decimals. it is further admitted that the plaintiffs have acquired 25 decimals of land and the defendants have acquired 18 decimals of land of the said 50 decimals. It is not disputed that the defendants purchased in 1976 and the plaintiffs purchased and took settlement of 25 decimals in 1979. So the admitted position is that the plaintiffs have been possessing 25 decimals since 1979 and the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 have been possessing 18 decimals since 1976. 

 6. We have perused the application as well as the plaint and the application for injunction. The plaintiffs have made some vague, unspecified and indefinite allegations stating that some portion of their land has been encroached by the defendants. But curiously enough either in the plaint or in the application for injunction no specific area or demarcation of the land which was allegedly encroached by the defendants has been given. Both the courts below considered this aspect in details and thereafter they came to a finding that since there is no specific area or demarcation of the land allegedly encroached by the defendants has been given in the application for injunctions, an order of temporary injunction can not be granted in such a case. So we do not find any reason to interfere with the above findings of the courts below inasmuch as we are also satisfied that the plaintiffs have not been able to make out any case of encroachment of any land by the defendants. 

 7. Mr. Ali Asgar further submits that in a partition suit injunction should be granted in view of the fact that if ultimately it is found that some portion of the plaintiff's land is encroached by the defendant, the plaintiffs will suffer irreparable loss and injury. He has referred to the case of Ram Bahadur Pal and others Vs. Rain Shankar Prankar Prasad Pal reported in ILR 27 (All) 688. We have gone through the above decision. In our view the above cited decision has no manner of application in the facts and circumstances of the present case because the principle laid down there is with regard to the land in rural areas, but in the instant case admittedly the land in question is situated within Faridpur Municipal area. So, we find that the above decision is of little assistance to Mr. Ali Asgar. On the other hand Mr. Md. Abdur Razzaque Miah, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite parties, has submitted that since the property in question is situated within the municipal area, even if it is a suit for partition, an injunction should not be granted in view of the fact that the construction of the building on the part of the said land is a development and not any damage to the suit land. In support of his contention he has referred to the case of Ali Ahmed Vs. Rezia Begum and others, BLD 1986, 326. In that case a Division Bench of this Court held that in a partition suit concerning land in the urban area a co-sharer should not be granted injunction if the construction proposed to be done by other co-sharers does not diminish the value of the suit land. Their Lordships of the Division Bench held as follows : 

 9. Mr. Razzaque further submits that the defendants are making their construction on northern portion of the suit land and they have not encroached upon any portion of the land belonging to the plaintiffs. Whether the defendants have actually encroached upon the land of the plaintiffs or not, it will be decided in the suit. Since it is a suit for partition against the co-sharers and the suit has been filed in 1986 and since then the dispute is going on between the parties it is desirable that the suit itself should be heard and disposed of as expeditiously as possible. In view of the facts and circumstances of the case, we find that the judgment and order of the lower Appellate Court do not call for any interference by this Court.
